body: This logic is dangerous. What if someone is making a website and they want to export a game to the root directory (but not to `index.html`)? The `index.html` could be a pre-existing file not created by Godot, and this code would destroy it.
I suggest backing up the existing `index.html` file to `index.html.old` if present.

I just added this code after playing with the new option, and after some test I saw an old index.html and I thought it could make it hard to know which is the .html file that you just exported (e.g game.html vs index.html)
I agree that is dangerous to remove it because it could be an intentional file on people export directory. I like the idea of renaming it to .old, but that could be also a problem if you get YOUR handcrafted index.html renamed every time.
Sadly, at the moment of writing this comment, I don't have any other idea. Besides of that I'm open to suggestions on this.
